editions.title: Pride and Prejudice
editions.author: Jane Austen
editions.edition: Hugh Thomson illustrated edition, 1894. Preface by George Saintsbury. Project Gutenberg 1342.
editions.description: Read the complete novel with Thomson’s drawings. An optional index finds words and phrases in the chapters you choose.

editions.title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
editions.author: Lewis Carroll
editions.edition: Arthur Rackham illustrations; proem by Austin Dobson. The source is an undated Heinemann / Doubleday, Page printing. Project Gutenberg 28885.
editions.description: Look at Rackham’s plates beside the scenes they illustrate, or take a seat at the Hatter’s table in Tea at Six.

editions.title: Walden & Civil Disobedience
editions.author: Henry David Thoreau
editions.edition: Walden and On the Duty of Civil Disobedience. Project Gutenberg 205; source updated 20 February 2026.
editions.description: See what the house and food accounts leave out. Inspect the pond survey beside Thoreau’s claims.

editions.title: Two lecture halls, one hour
editions.author: Hegel & Schopenhauer
editions.edition: Hegel’s Lectures on the History of Philosophy, complete volume 1 of 3, translated by E. S. Haldane; Schopenhauer’s The Art of Controversy and the other essays in the selected T. Bailey Saunders collection. Project Gutenberg 51635 and 10731. Saunders’s own omissions are retained and disclosed in this edition.
editions.description: Compare their arguments about disagreement, winning and borrowed judgment. The paired readings come from later publications; the lecture halls are an editorial setting.
editions.editionLabel: Hegel: E. S. Haldane · Schopenhauer: T. Bailey Saunders

editions.title: The Odyssey
editions.author: Homer
editions.edition: Samuel Butler’s prose translation, 1900, with Henry Festing Jones’s second preface, 1921. Project Gutenberg 1727.
editions.feature: A voyage home. A bag of winds.
editions.description: Read the complete Butler translation, then steer the boat in Homeward, a short game drawing on episodes from the poem.

editions.title: Dracula
editions.author: Bram Stoker
editions.edition: Complete English novel with source front and back matter, cover and publisher colophon. Project Gutenberg 345.
editions.description: Compare the Demeter’s log with accounts of its arrival in the Whitby Papers, or try to escape five castle rooms in the game.

editions.title: At Table
editions.author: Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin · Isabella Beeton · Rufus Estes
editions.edition: Three complete selected digital texts: Robinson’s Brillat-Savarin translation, Beeton’s Household Management and Estes’s 1911 Good Things to Eat. The Robinson witness omits two French meditations; Beeton’s digital text supplies illustration descriptions, without the engravings.
editions.description: Compare asparagus, stock and coffee across a gastronome’s stories, a household manual and a professional cook’s recipes. An optional reading follows Estes’s work, wages and authorship.

editions.title: The Inward Life
editions.author: Julian of Norwich · Rabindranath Tagore · William James
editions.edition: Revelations of Divine Love, Grace Warrack’s 1901 version; Sādhanā, the English witness dated 1916 with its credited collaborators; The Varieties of Religious Experience, twenty-eighth impression, 1917.
editions.feature: What makes an experience feel true?
editions.description: Put James’s account of mystical states beside Julian’s years of interpretation and Tagore’s daily worship. A second study follows the editing and translation of these English texts.
editions.editionLabel: Julian of Norwich in Grace Warrack’s version

editions.title: What Can Music Say?
editions.author: Eduard Hanslick · Leo Tolstoy
editions.edition: The Beautiful in Music, Gustav Cohen’s translation of the seventh German edition in the 1891-dated scan witness; What Is Art?, Aylmer Maude’s 1904 witness. Historical notation and full source apparatus accompany the texts.
editions.description: Hanslick and Tolstoy both find difficulties in Beethoven’s Ninth. Read the passages together and examine the different things each critic asks music to do.
editions.editionLabel: Hanslick: Gustav Cohen · Tolstoy: Aylmer Maude

editions.title: Learning to See
editions.author: John Ruskin · Walter Crane
editions.edition: The complete selected English digital editions of The Elements of Drawing and Line & Form, including 218 source illustrations, notes and indexes.
editions.description: Look closely at Crane’s two olive branches beside Ruskin’s attention to boughs and white intervals. An optional workbench lets you adjust a repeating sprig and inspect its joins.

editions.title: Beside the Bed
editions.author: Florence Nightingale · Walt Whitman
editions.edition: Notes on Nursing, Appleton 1898; the complete Specimen Days extracted from Gutenberg’s Complete Prose Works, with its notes and verse. Historical nursing is read as literary and social evidence.
editions.description: Follow preparations, messages, conversation and departure through two accounts of visiting the sick. An optional close reading compares a whispered corridor with a singing ward.

editions.title: The Alps
editions.author: Martin Conway · A. D. McCormick
editions.edition: The complete 1904 text by Martin Conway, with all seventy colour illustrations by A. D. McCormick. Project Gutenberg 39542 and the University of Toronto scan of the printed volume.
editions.description: Compare Conway’s visitor and climber looking at the Jungfrau, or examine McCormick’s two paintings of Pallanza.

editions.title: Nietzsche in company
editions.author: Friedrich Nietzsche · Epicurus
editions.edition: The complete Joyful Wisdom, including its verse, in the 1910 English edition; Epicurus’s complete Letter to Menoeceus in C. D. Yonge’s translation. Project Gutenberg 52124 and 57342.
editions.description: Read Nietzsche’s account of Epicurus beside the letter itself, then compare it with Nietzsche’s later judgment.
editions.editionLabel: Nietzsche’s prose: Thomas Common · Epicurus: C. D. Yonge

editions.title: War and Peace
editions.author: Leo Tolstoy
editions.edition: The complete Maude translation: fifteen books and both epilogues. Twelve plates from the illustrated album published for Sever in 1893 accompany the text.
editions.description: Open the pictures as you reach their chapters, with a guide to the opening cast and notes on names and dates.

editions.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
editions.author: Frederick Douglass
editions.edition: Boston, Anti-Slavery Office, 1845. Complete Narrative with original front matter and Appendix; UNC Documenting the American South. Three separately identified historical documents accompany Chapters VII and XI.
editions.description: Read the 1845 Narrative beside the schoolbook Douglass recalled, the 1793 law and his later account of escape.

editions.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
editions.author: Edgar Allan Poe
editions.edition: Tales, Wiley & Putnam, 1845, pp. 64–82. Beardsley’s 1894 drawing and Clarke’s 1919 illustration, reproduced from a Duke copy catalogued 1923.
editions.description: Compare Beardsley and Clarke with Poe’s words. Follow the story into film and music, with the ending kept behind a reveal.

editions.title: Ballads and a play
editions.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe · Friedrich Schiller · Gottfried August Bürger
editions.edition: Five complete ballads and Goethe’s complete Iphigenie auf Tauris. Original German with separate historical English translations; each witness and transcription license is identified.
editions.description: Read Goethe, Schiller and Bürger in German and English. Compare stanzas and speaker turns; follow two close readings of refusal and gesture.

editions.title: A kingdom for a stage
editions.author: William Shakespeare
editions.edition: Complete Julius Caesar, Henry V and The Tempest. Folger editions, edited by Barbara Mowat and Paul Werstine, licensed CC BY-NC 3.0; source matter and apparatus retained.
editions.feature: Three plays, and the world around them.
editions.description: Read with notes on Rome, kingship and the playhouse. Inspect stage directions and a later picture of Miranda.

editions.title: Pictures after dark
editions.author: Victor Hugo · Aloysius Bertrand
editions.edition: Eight complete works, in French and historical English. Selected 1890 illustrations by Henry W. McVickar; optional Baudelaire comparison and separately credited Hugo and Callot images.
editions.editionLabel: French with O’Sullivan, Merrill and Lang
editions.feature: An open window. A closed one.
editions.description: Compare French and English, inspect the illustrated pages, and read Bertrand beside Baudelaire.

editions.title: Caesar and the emperors
editions.author: Caesar · Augustus · Marcus Aurelius
editions.edition: Caesar’s Gallic War VII, all of Augustus’s Res Gestae with its later Summary, and Meditations II–III. Selected Sallust, Tacitus and Pliny–Trajan correspondence provide other accounts.
editions.description: Read a campaign, a public record and an emperor’s private reflections. Compare rival accounts and inspect historical siege plans.

editions.title: Antigone
editions.author: Sophocles
editions.edition: The complete play in Richard Claverhouse Jebb’s prose translation: 1904 collection, 1917 reprint. Adapted Wikisource encoding retains its contributor credits and CC BY-SA 4.0 terms.
editions.feature: Creon forbids the burial. Antigone does it anyway.
editions.description: Read Jebb’s complete play. In A public stain, compare Creon’s order with the prophet’s warning. The optional study includes the ending.

editions.title: A Doll’s House
editions.author: Henrik Ibsen
editions.edition: William Archer’s translation in Heinemann’s 1909 printing. Complete cast, setting and three acts, with seven historical notes; the collected volume’s introductions and Ghosts are excluded.
editions.feature: A play laid out to be spoken.
editions.description: Read Ibsen as a working script, with speakers beside their lines, clear stage directions and direct routes to each act.

editions.title: The Book of Tea
editions.author: Okakura Kakuzō
editions.edition: Seven essays, original English, checked against the 1906 G. P. Putnam’s Sons witness. Includes the dedication, detailed contents, ten source notes and original verse lineation.
editions.description: Read Okakura on tea, art and hospitality. Make a cup with sourced sencha, black-tea and matcha methods, and an adjustable infusion timer.
